bank-credit-by-the-shift.label: Credit by the shift
bank-credit-by-the-shift.title: Reading a loan before you take it
bank-credit-by-the-shift.body:
Ogiso's Bank and Ogiso's Register anchor the system's formal credit records. Around them, station lenders offer their own terms: registered houses may ask for standing, while independent counters may ask fewer questions and charge more. A ship or apartment may have a purchase mortgage; a cash loan adds another mortgage line to the ledger.

Check who holds the debt, what the shift schedule says, and what remains outstanding before signing. A lender's interest charge is separate from a late fee on an unpaid bill. The ledger adds the late fee at each shift change until the bill is paid. Letters can remind or explain; they do not move money. Use the Finances window to pay and to check what remains due. A smaller down payment does not make the purchase cost less overall.
